title: Pandas Waste 83% of Their Bamboo. Why? 🐼
description:
Why do pandas eat bamboo all day? Giant pandas have a carnivore's short, simple gut, so they digest only about 17% of their bamboo and survive by eating up to 14 hours a day and saving energy with a slow thyroid and lots of rest.

Sources:
https://www.livescience.com/50871-pandas-gut-bacteria-bamboo-digestion.html
https://phys.org/news/2015-07-under-active-pandas-energy-sloths.html
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3144909

Animated in the Kawaii Anime style.

topic: The Panda Paradox: why does a meat-eater's body live on bamboo?
script:
Pandas waste eighty-three percent of the bamboo they eat.
Here's why you never see it.
Inside, a panda has a meat-eater's gut,
built just like a bear's:
short, simple intestines,
and no cow-style stomach chambers.
So bamboo rushes straight through,
and most of it comes out in less than a day.
So pandas eat for up to fourteen hours a day,
crunching up to thirty-eight kilos of bamboo.
And they save energy like a phone on low battery.
Their thyroid runs slow,
their brain and liver are small,
and they nap a lot.
A panda burns barely forty percent of the energy
you'd expect for its size.
Scientists think it all started
when their ancestors lost a gene
for tasting meat's savory flavor.
Could you eat just one food every day, like a panda?
key_facts: Giant pandas digest only about 17% of the bamboo they eat (so ~83% passes through)
Pandas have a short, simple carnivore-type gut and gut microbes like other bears
Food passes through in under a day
Pandas eat up to ~14 hours a day, up to ~38 kg (84 lb) of bamboo
A 2015 Science study found pandas use about 38% of the energy expected for their size, with low thyroid hormone and small brain, liver and kidneys
Pandas' umami (meat taste) receptor gene Tas1r1 became a pseudogene
